summary.intent: Capture implementation decisions for Phase 21 (BYO-IPFS Node Support) via discuss-phase, then run plan-phase to generate research, validation strategy, and UI design contract.
summary.outcome: CONTEXT.md was created with key architectural decisions (client-direct pinning, three-mode model, TEE-based migration, PSA+Kubo support). Research, validation strategy, and UI-SPEC were generated, though the UI-SPEC required one revision cycle due to a Dimension 5 (Spacing) issue.

repo: BYO-IPFS originally planned as server-relay for v1.1, client-direct for v1.2 (PROJECT.md), but the session revised this to client-direct in v1.1 since the SDK already exists.
The TEE (Phala Cloud) is already used for IPNS republishing background jobs and can be reused for pin migration — it handles opaque encrypted blobs without seeing plaintext content.
Auth token storage for BYO-IPFS will follow the same pattern as IPNS keys: client encrypts with TEE public key, TEE decrypts in-enclave.
The existing IpfsProvider interface and local.provider.ts are the integration points for adding a RemotePinningProvider at the SDK layer.
Quota tracking is advisory (no enforcement) for BYO-IPFS — CipherBox API receives lightweight CID registration only.
ROADMAP.md SC#2 and BYO-02 need updating to reflect revised scope (three-mode pinning model + client-direct instead of server-relay dual-pin).

Captures locked decisions: three-mode pinning, client-direct arch, TEE migration, PSA+Kubo auto-detection, STORAGE tab UI pattern

workflow: The discuss-phase workflow surfaces architectural assumptions early — the session caught a fundamental conflict between PROJECT.md's server-relay plan and the user's zero-knowledge requirement before any code was written.
TEE reuse for new background job types (pin migration) is a valid pattern when the job only needs opaque CIDs and encrypted credentials — no plaintext exposure.
UI-SPEC checker revision loop worked as designed: one blocking issue in Dimension 5 (Spacing) triggered an automatic researcher re-spawn without user intervention.

friction: The UI-SPEC failed the checker on the first pass (Dimension 5 — Spacing), requiring a revision iteration before the session transcript ends.
The plan-phase UI design contract gate interrupted the planning flow and required a separate /gsd:ui-phase invocation before /gsd:plan-phase could continue.
The original PROJECT.md spec (server-relay v1.1) conflicted with the user's zero-knowledge requirement, requiring an architectural pivot mid-discussion.
